questions.question: Wular Lake is South Asia's largest freshwater lake. Approximately how large is it?
Wular Lake is fed by which river?
Wular Lake was designated a Ramsar Wetland in which year?
The Wular Lake's area has shrunk dramatically from its historic size due to?
options: Encroachment for agriculture, willow plantation, and silt accumulation

questions.question: Wular Lake supports the livelihood of which community primarily?
options: Kashmiri fishermen and aquatic plant harvesters

pins.summary: Wular Lake in Jammu & Kashmir is South Asia's largest freshwater lake at approximately 189 sq km — though its historic area was over 400 sq km before encroachment for agriculture, willow plantation, and silt accumulation dramatically reduced it. Fed by the Jhelum River, Wular is a Ramsar Wetland since 1981 and a critical habitat for migratory waterfowl. The lake supports thousands of Kashmiri fishermen and aquatic plant harvesters who collect singara (water chestnuts) and nadru (lotus stems). The Tulbul Navigation Project (India) and Wular Barrage Project have been a source of India-Pakistan dispute, with Pakistan claiming they violate the Indus Waters Treaty.

questions.question: Tso Moriri is a high-altitude lake in Ladakh at approximately what elevation?
Tso Moriri is a Ramsar Wetland. It is the breeding ground for which rare bird?
The Black-necked Crane is sacred to which communities?
Tso Moriri has no outflow — it is an endorheic (closed) lake. This means its water?
options: Flows into the Indus via an underground channel
Only leaves through evaporation, making it slightly saline
Is completely freshwater despite no outflow

questions.question: The Korzok village on Tso Moriri's shores is one of India's highest permanent settlements at approximately?

pins.summary: Tso Moriri ('Mountain Lake') in the Changthang plateau of Ladakh sits at 4,522 metres — one of the world's highest Ramsar Wetlands. As an endorheic lake (no outflow), its water leaves only through evaporation, giving it slightly saline water. The lake is the primary breeding ground in India for the Black-necked Crane — considered sacred by Tibetan Buddhists and one of the world's rarest crane species. The Korzok Monastery on its northern shore, home to the nomadic Changpa community, marks one of India's highest permanently inhabited settlements. The Changpa's Pashmina goats — source of the world's finest Cashmere wool — graze the surrounding high-altitude pastures.

questions.question: The Konkan Coast stretches along which states?
The Konkan coast is known for which distinctive geographic feature formed by the Western Ghats meeting the sea?
options: A narrow coastal strip between the Western Ghats escarpment and the Arabian Sea

questions.question: Which crop is the Konkan coast most famous for?
The Ratnagiri and Devgad districts of Maharashtra produce which GI-tagged mango variety?
The Konkan region was historically important for which maritime tradition?
options: The Angre (Kanhoji Angre) naval power that challenged European dominance in the 18th century

pins.summary: The Konkan coast — the narrow strip between the Western Ghats' sheer escarpment and the Arabian Sea — runs through Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, and Kerala. The Ghats' abrupt descent to the sea creates one of the wettest coastal environments on Earth during the monsoon, nurturing the famous Alphonso (Hapus) mango. Ratnagiri and Devgad districts of Maharashtra produce the GI-tagged Alphonso — considered the world's finest mango variety, commanding premium prices globally. The 18th-century Maratha admiral Kanhoji Angre controlled the Konkan coast and repeatedly defeated Dutch, English, and Portuguese fleets — representing one of the most successful naval challenges to European maritime dominance in Asian history.

questions.question: Bhitarkanika is India's second-largest mangrove ecosystem after?
Bhitarkanika National Park is a Ramsar Wetland and is famous for housing India's largest population of?
The Gahirmatha Marine Sanctuary adjacent to Bhitarkanika hosts the world's largest nesting of which turtle?
The mass nesting phenomenon of Olive Ridley turtles is called?
The Bhitarkanika area is at the delta of which rivers?
options: All of the above — multiple river mouths

pins.summary: Bhitarkanika in Odisha — India's second-largest mangrove ecosystem — sits at the delta of the Brahmani and Baitarani rivers. Its national park contains India's largest population of saltwater crocodiles (the world's largest living reptile, reaching up to 6 metres). Adjacent Gahirmatha Marine Sanctuary is the world's largest Olive Ridley sea turtle rookery — during the annual mass nesting (arribada) phenomenon, hundreds of thousands of females come ashore simultaneously to nest, creating one of nature's most spectacular events. The 1999 Super Cyclone caused massive damage to Bhitarkanika, but the mangroves also significantly buffered the impact on inland communities — a powerful demonstration of natural coastal protection.

questions.question: The Indira Gandhi Canal is India's longest irrigation canal. How long is it?
The canal draws water from which river via the Harike Barrage?
options: Sutlej and Beas rivers (combined at Harike)

questions.question: The canal transformed which part of Rajasthan from desert into agricultural land?
options: Northern Rajasthan (Thar Desert — particularly Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Barmer districts)

questions.question: While transforming the Thar, the canal has also caused which unintended ecological problem?
options: Waterlogging and soil salinity in command areas

questions.question: The canal was originally called the Rajasthan Canal before being renamed after which Prime Minister?

pins.summary: The Indira Gandhi Canal — India's longest irrigation canal at 1,422 km including its distribution network — draws water from the Sutlej-Beas system via the Harike Barrage and carries it into the heart of the Thar Desert, transforming millions of hectares in Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Sri Ganganagar, and Barmer districts from desert into agricultural land. Originally the Rajasthan Canal, it was renamed after Indira Gandhi who championed its completion. While dramatically improving agricultural productivity and reducing poverty in northwest Rajasthan, the project has also caused waterlogging and soil salinity in its command areas — a common problem with large irrigation schemes when drainage is inadequate. The canal remains one of independent India's most transformative water infrastructure projects.

questions.question: Who built the Jantar Mantar observatories?
How many Jantar Mantar observatories did Jai Singh II build across India?
The Samrat Yantra at Jaipur's Jantar Mantar is the world's largest stone sundial. Its gnomon (shadow-casting arm) is approximately how tall?
Jantar Mantar Jaipur became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in which year?
The instruments at Jantar Mantar were built to accomplish which primary scientific purpose?
options: Accurately calculating astronomical positions, time, and compiling astronomical tables
Determining auspicious dates for royal events

pins.summary: The Jantar Mantar observatory in Jaipur — UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2010 — is the largest and best-preserved of five such observatories built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II (also the founder of Jaipur) in the early 18th century. Jai Singh, a passionate astronomer who found existing astronomical tables inaccurate, built massive masonry instruments that could make precise naked-eye astronomical measurements. The Samrat Yantra (Supreme Instrument) — a 27-metre triangular gnomon — can measure time to within two seconds and still accurately tracks the sun's position. Jai Singh also translated European and Arabic astronomical texts and corresponded with the Portuguese king — making him one of the pre-telescope era's most sophisticated astronomers.

questions.question: Chettinad mansions were built by which trading community?
The Chettiars built these mansions primarily between which years, from wealth earned where?
options: 1600-1700, from local trade in Tamil Nadu
1850-1930, from money lending and trade across Southeast Asia (Burma, Malaysia, Ceylon)

questions.question: A distinctive feature of Chettinad mansion construction is the use of which unusual flooring material?
options: Egg whites mixed with limestone to create a smooth polished floor

questions.question: Chettinad mansions typically face which direction and have which central feature?
options: South, with a large banyan tree
East, with a large open courtyard (thinnai and multiple inner courtyards)
North, with a prayer room facing the Himalayas

questions.question: The Chettinad region is also famous for which culinary tradition?
options: Chettinad cuisine — one of India's most complex spice-heavy culinary traditions
Street food culture similar to Mumbai

pins.summary: Chettinad in Tamil Nadu's Sivaganga district contains one of India's most extraordinary concentrations of heritage architecture — hundreds of palatial mansions built by the Nattukotai Chettiars (Nagarathar), a Tamil trading community that accumulated enormous wealth through money-lending and trade across British Burma, Ceylon, Malaysia, and Singapore between 1850 and 1930. The mansions, some with 100+ rooms, incorporate materials from across the world — Burma teak, Belgian glass, Italian marble — combined with local craftsmanship. Their distinctive egg-white lime flooring, polished to a mirror finish, and layered inner courtyards create unique domestic spaces. As the Chettiar community declined and emigrated, many mansions stand empty — a UNESCO-watched endangered heritage category.

questions.question: The Rock Garden of Chandigarh was secretly created by which person over many years?
options: Nek Chand Saini — a road inspector in Chandigarh
An American sculptor who worked in Le Corbusier's team

questions.question: Nek Chand built the Rock Garden from?
options: Industrial and urban waste — broken bangles, ceramics, electrical equipment, bathroom fittings

questions.question: When authorities discovered the Rock Garden (built illegally on government land), they?
options: Initially planned demolition but public outcry saved it — it became a government-owned public space
Adopted it immediately as a tourist site

questions.question: The Rock Garden is now one of the most visited sites in India. How many visitors does it receive annually?
Nek Chand's Rock Garden is cited internationally as a leading example of which artistic tradition?

pins.summary: The Rock Garden of Chandigarh — created secretly over 18 years by road inspector Nek Chand Saini beginning in 1957 — is one of the world's most remarkable examples of outsider art. Working clandestinely on government land (and thus illegally), Nek Chand built an elaborate fantasy kingdom of sculptures, waterfalls, and pathways using nothing but industrial and urban waste: broken bangles, ceramic tiles, discarded electrical equipment, and bathroom fixtures. When authorities discovered the 12-acre site in 1975, they initially planned demolition — but a massive public response led to its protection and formalisation as a paid tourist attraction. Now receiving over 1.2 million visitors annually, it is Chandigarh's most visited site and is cited in art circles worldwide as a masterwork of Art Brut.

location.name: Basilica of Bom Jesus — Old Goa

questions.question: The Basilica of Bom Jesus enshrines the remains of which Christian saint?
options: St. Thomas (who brought Christianity to India)
St. Francis Xavier — Jesuit missionary to Asia

questions.question: The Basilica was built by the Portuguese in which year?
St. Francis Xavier's remains are displayed publicly every how many years in a ceremony called the Exposition?
Old Goa's churches and convents became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in which year?
The style of the Basilica of Bom Jesus is?

pins.summary: The Basilica of Bom Jesus ('Good Jesus') in Old Goa, completed in 1605, is one of India's most significant Christian heritage sites and part of UNESCO's 'Churches and Convents of Goa' World Heritage Site (1986). It enshrines the remains of St. Francis Xavier — the Jesuit missionary who brought Christianity to India, Japan, and other parts of Asia in the 16th century — in an ornate silver reliquary donated by the Florentine sculptor Giovanni Battista Foggini. Every ten years, the saint's body is displayed to the public in an 'Exposition' that draws millions of pilgrims from across the Catholic world. Old Goa's baroque churches, built at the height of Portuguese colonial power, represent the finest Portuguese colonial religious architecture outside Portugal.

questions.question: The Venkateswara Temple at Tirupati is the world's most visited religious site. Approximately how many pilgrims visit annually?
The temple is also the world's richest religious institution by annual income. It receives approximately how much in donations per year?
Devotees who visit Tirupati often donate what as an offering?
options: Their hair (tonsuring — the hair is then auctioned to wig manufacturers globally)

questions.question: Lord Venkateswara at Tirupati is a form of which deity?
The Tirumala hills on which the temple stands are part of which hill range?

pins.summary: The Venkateswara Temple at Tirumala-Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh's Eastern Ghats is the world's most visited religious site — receiving an estimated 75,000–100,000 pilgrims daily (over 75 million annually) who come to worship Lord Venkateswara, a form of Vishnu. It is simultaneously the world's wealthiest religious institution, receiving over ₹12,000 crore annually in donations — including the famous hair donations: pilgrims tonsure their heads as an offering, and the temple auctions the hair to European and American wig manufacturers, generating substantial revenue. The Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) manages the temple complex and is one of India's largest non-governmental employers, providing education, healthcare, and food (the famous Tirupati laddoo) to millions.

questions.question: Amul is India's largest food products organisation. What does AMUL stand for?
Amul was founded in 1946 as part of which movement?
options: The cooperative dairy movement led by Tribhuvandas Patel and Verghese Kurien
The White Revolution under Lal Bahadur Shastri

questions.question: Verghese Kurien, often called the 'Father of the White Revolution,' created which national dairy development programme?
options: Operation Flood — the world's largest dairy development programme

questions.question: The Amul cooperative model is unique because?
options: The government owns and operates it
It is owned by 3.6 million milk producer members — mostly small and marginal farmers
It is owned by large dairy farmers only

questions.question: India is now the world's largest milk producer. Its annual milk production is approximately?

pins.summary: Amul (Anand Milk Union Limited), founded in 1946 in Anand, Gujarat, is one of the world's most successful cooperative enterprises and the cornerstone of India's dairy revolution. Under Verghese Kurien ('Milkman of India'), Amul became the model for Operation Flood (1970-1996) — the world's largest dairy development programme, which transformed India from a milk-deficient country into the world's largest milk producer (now approximately 220 million tonnes annually). Amul is owned by 3.6 million farmer members across 18,700 village cooperatives — most of them smallholders with 2-3 buffaloes — who collectively created a national brand that successfully competed against multinationals. The Amul cooperative model is studied globally as a template for inclusive rural development.

questions.question: Visakhapatnam Port is India's fourth-largest port. It is India's only?
options: Natural harbour on the eastern coast with deep drafts
Government-owned port with private terminal operators

questions.question: The Visakhapatnam Steel Plant nearby is India's only what type of plant?
The Eastern Naval Command of the Indian Navy is based in?
India's first nuclear submarine (INS Arihant) is based at which location?
The annual storm that devastated Visakhapatnam in 2014 — Cyclone Hudhud — caused approximately what damage?

pins.summary: Visakhapatnam ('Vizag') in Andhra Pradesh is India's most strategically significant eastern port city. The port is one of the few natural deep-water harbours on India's east coast. The Eastern Naval Command, headquartered at Vizag, is responsible for India's entire eastern seaboard and the Bay of Bengal — and it is the base for INS Arihant, India's first nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN), built at the Ship Building Centre in a highly classified programme. Vizag's industrial complex includes the Shore-Based Integrated Steel Plant (RINL), the HPCL refinery, and a pharmaceutical cluster. Cyclone Hudhud in 2014 caused over ₹21,000 crore damage to the city — one of India's costliest urban cyclone disasters.

questions.question: Surat is called the 'Silk City' and handles what percentage of India's synthetic textile production?
Surat's textile industry processes primarily which type of fabric?
options: Synthetic fabrics (polyester, nylon) — Surat is the world's largest producer of polyester fabric

questions.question: Surat was one of the major ports of the Mughal Empire. The British East India Company established its first Indian factory in Surat in which year?
Surat Diamond Bourse, opened in 2023, is the world's largest commercial building by floor space, surpassing?
The 1994 plague that struck Surat caused mass migration and international concern. The city's subsequent transformation into one of India's cleanest cities was led by?
options: Commissioner S.R. Rao's comprehensive municipal reform programme

pins.summary: Surat is India's fastest-growing major city — a global textile and diamond hub that has reinvented itself multiple times. The city processes over 60% of India's synthetic textiles (primarily polyester fabric) and 90% of the world's rough diamonds. The British East India Company established its first Indian factory in Surat in 1612, making it the starting point of British India. The 1994 bubonic plague outbreak triggered mass exodus and international stigma — but also a remarkable urban transformation under Municipal Commissioner S.R. Rao, who reformed garbage collection, drainage, and sanitation so thoroughly that Surat now consistently ranks among India's cleanest cities. The Surat Diamond Bourse (2023), the world's largest commercial building by floor space (surpassing the Pentagon), consolidates the diamond trade that employs 700,000 workers.

questions.question: Rourkela Steel Plant was built with assistance from which country?
Rourkela Steel Plant was established during which Five Year Plan as one of India's flagship industrial projects?
Rourkela is primarily known for producing which type of steel products?
Which NIT (National Institute of Technology) was established alongside Rourkela Steel Plant to supply engineers?
The river on which Rourkela is located is?

pins.summary: Rourkela Steel Plant in Odisha — established during the Second Five Year Plan with West German technical and financial assistance, commissioned in 1959 — is one of the three iconic public sector steel plants built by Nehru's government to kickstart India's industrial revolution (alongside Bhilai with Soviet help and Durgapur with British assistance). Rourkela specialises in flat products (plates, coils, sheets) used in shipbuilding, automotive, and construction sectors. The plant township also became the site of the Regional Engineering College (now NIT Rourkela) — the government's recognition that an industrial complex needed a technical training institution alongside it. The Brahmani River provides the plant's water supply.

questions.question: The Assam Gas Cracker Project at Lepetkata produces which chemical from natural gas?
Assam's Digboi has which historical distinction?
options: India's oldest oil refinery (1901) and the site of Asia's first oil well
India's oldest railway line outside Bengal

questions.question: The Northeast Gas Grid aims to connect all eight northeastern states. Its primary fuel source for the region is?
options: Natural gas from Tripura and Assam gas fields

questions.question: Brahmaputra Cracker and Polymer Limited (BCPL) at Lepetkata is a joint venture between which entities?
options: GAIL, Oil India, NRL, and the Government of Assam

questions.question: The northeast India region is significant for energy because it has?
options: Significant oil, natural gas, and hydropower resources — but infrastructure has historically been inadequate to exploit them
The only viable nuclear fuel (thorium) deposits

pins.summary: Northeast India's energy resources — natural gas in Tripura and Assam, vast hydropower potential in Arunachal Pradesh and other states, and significant oil from Assam's Digboi fields (site of Asia's first oil well, 1889, and India's oldest refinery, 1901) — have historically been underutilised due to inadequate infrastructure and geographical isolation. The Assam Gas Cracker Project (BCPL) at Lepetkata, a joint venture between GAIL, Oil India, NRL, and the Assam government, converts natural gas into polymers (plastics) — the region's first petrochemical plant. The North East Gas Grid initiative aims to provide all eight northeastern states with piped natural gas supply, reducing dependence on expensive LPG cylinders and supporting industrial development.

questions.question: Eid ul-Adha commemorates which event from Islamic tradition?
options: The Prophet's night journey to heaven
Ibrahim's (Abraham's) willingness to sacrifice his son as commanded by God

questions.question: The ritual sacrifice (Qurbani) on Eid ul-Adha involves?
options: Sacrificing a goat, sheep, cow, or camel — with the meat distributed to family, neighbours, and the poor
A symbolic 'sacrifice' with no actual animal slaughter

questions.question: Lucknow is famous for its distinctive Nawabi culture. The Nawabs of Lucknow were from which dynasty?
Lucknow's 'Tehzeeb' (culture of refinement) is expressed through which art form unique to the city?
options: Kathak dance, Nawabi cuisine (biryani, korma), Chikankari embroidery, and Urdu poetry

questions.question: The Bara Imambara in Lucknow, built in 1784, is famous for which architectural feature?
options: Its height — tallest building in colonial India
Its central hall (asafi hall) — one of the world's largest arched chambers without any supporting beams

pins.summary: Lucknow — capital of Uttar Pradesh and the historic seat of the Nawabs of Awadh — is India's most refined Urdu and Islamic cultural centre. The Nawabi culture of 'Tehzeeb' (refinement and courtesy) shaped Lucknow's distinctive identity: its Kathak dance tradition, its cuisine (Biryani, Galouti kebab, Nihari), its Chikankari embroidery, and its Urdu poetry. The Bara Imambara (1784), built by Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula during a famine as a public works project to employ the poor, contains one of the world's largest arched halls without supporting beams — and the labyrinthine 'Bhool Bhulaiya' (maze) within its upper galleries. During Eid ul-Adha, Lucknow's old city celebrations combine Islamic tradition with the distinctive Lucknawi refinement that softens festival customs.

questions.question: Bonalu is a festival of which Telugu community celebrated primarily in Hyderabad and Telangana?
options: Specifically Telangana communities — a folk festival honouring the Mother Goddess Mahankali

questions.question: The word 'Bonalu' derives from the Telugu word for?
options: Offering (of cooked rice and other food in a pot)

questions.question: Bonalu celebrates the return of the Goddess after preventing which calamity?
options: The plague that struck Hyderabad in 1813

questions.question: The procession during Bonalu features women balancing pots (Bonam) on their heads. These pots contain?
options: Cooked rice, curd, and jaggery — an offering to the goddess

questions.question: Bonalu is primarily celebrated at which Hyderabad temple?

pins.summary: Bonalu — a traditional Telangana folk festival celebrated over three weekends in the Telugu months of Ashadha and Shravan (July-August) — honours the Mother Goddess Mahankali. The festival originated in Secunderabad's Ujjaini Mahankali Temple to thank the goddess for ending the plague of 1813. Women dress in red, balance decorated pots (Bonam) filled with cooked rice, curd, and jaggery on their heads, and walk in procession to the temple. The Rangam (oracle) — a priest who goes into a trance and delivers prophecies from the Goddess — is a dramatic and spiritually significant element. Bonalu was declared Telangana's state festival in 2014 when the new state was formed, asserting a distinct Telangana cultural identity.

questions.question: Dilli Haat in New Delhi was established to give craftspeople direct market access without?
options: Middlemen who typically take a large share of the retail price

questions.question: Dilli Haat features crafts from how many Indian states?
The GI (Geographical Indication) tag protects traditional Indian crafts. Which of these is a GI-tagged craft?
options: Kanjivaram silk saree from Tamil Nadu

questions.question: India's handloom sector employs approximately how many people, making it the second-largest employer after agriculture?
Which Indian state has the highest number of GI-tagged products?

pins.summary: Dilli Haat — established in 1994 in New Delhi — is India's most successful model for giving traditional craftspeople direct access to urban consumers, eliminating middlemen who typically capture 60-70% of retail value. The haat rotates craftspeople from all 28 states and 8 Union Territories through its stalls, creating a permanent showcase of India's extraordinary craft diversity. India's traditional crafts sector employs approximately 43 lakh (4.3 million) artisans — the second-largest employment sector after agriculture — but faces existential threats from cheap machine-made imitations. The GI (Geographical Indication) tag system, modelled on European protections for products like Champagne and Parma ham, protects Indian crafts including Kanjivaram silk, Pashmina, Darjeeling tea, and Kolhapuri chappals. Tamil Nadu has the most GI-tagged products of any Indian state.

questions.question: The Kalbelia dance is performed by which Rajasthani community?
The Kalbelia dance was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in which year?
The most celebrated Kalbelia dancer who brought international fame to the tradition was?
The Kalbelia costume for women is distinctive for being entirely?
options: Black with silver and mirror embroidery

questions.question: The Kalbelia community traditionally made their living as?
options: Snake charmers and traders of snake venom and traditional medicine

pins.summary: The Kalbelia dance — UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage since 2010 — originates with the Kalbelia community of Rajasthan, traditionally snake charmers and traders of snake-related traditional medicines. As snake charming became illegal and marginalised, the Kalbelia community's survival strategy pivoted to their dance tradition. The Kalbelia dance mimics the sinuous movements of a serpent — women in distinctive black embroidered costumes spin with extraordinary speed and grace while male musicians play the been (pungi flute) and dholak drum. Gulabi Sapera, the community's most celebrated dancer, brought Kalbelia to international stages in the 1990s-2000s, transforming a marginalised community's tradition into a globally recognised art form.

questions.question: Chhath Puja is dedicated to which deity?
options: Surya (the Sun God) and Chhathi Maiya (Goddess Usha)

questions.question: Chhath Puja is unique among Hindu festivals because?
options: It is performed on riverbanks facing the setting and rising sun — no priest or idol is required
It is performed only by men

questions.question: Chhath Puja lasts for how many days?
Chhath is primarily associated with which states?
options: Bihar, Jharkhand, UP and the diaspora wherever Bihari communities settle

questions.question: The prasad offered during Chhath includes which food item made from jaggery and wheat?

pins.summary: Chhath Puja — Bihar's most important festival — is a four-day worship of Surya (the Sun God) and Chhathi Maiya that requires no temple, no priest, and no idol. Devotees (primarily women) observe rigorous fasting for 36 hours and stand in rivers or ponds at sunset and sunrise to offer arghya (water offerings) directly to the sun. The festival's most photographed moment — thousands of devotees standing waist-deep in the Ganga at Patna or the Yamuna at Delhi's banks, holding traditional baskets of prasad, as the orange sun touches the horizon — is one of India's most powerful visual spectacles. Chhath has spread wherever Bihari and Purvanchali communities have migrated — from Mauritius to the USA, the festival is celebrated wherever these diasporas settle.

questions.question: Andhra Pradesh was bifurcated in which year to create Telangana?
The proposed new capital Amaravati is planned on the banks of which river?
Ancient Amaravati (near the proposed capital) was famous for which Buddhist monument?
options: The Amaravati Stupa — one of ancient India's greatest Buddhist structures

questions.question: Andhra Pradesh has India's longest coastline. Approximately how long is it?
After losing Hyderabad to Telangana, Andhra Pradesh's executive capital functions are being conducted from?
options: Amaravati (partially) and Visakhapatnam as an alternative

pins.summary: Andhra Pradesh's bifurcation in 2014 — creating Telangana — was one of independent India's most contentious state reorganisations. Losing Hyderabad to Telangana left Andhra Pradesh without a capital. The proposed new capital Amaravati on the Krishna River — named after the nearby ancient Buddhist site where the Amaravati Stupa (2nd century BCE) once stood — became a major political flashpoint: one government planned it as a global-standard new city, the next scaled it back dramatically. The capital question remains partially unresolved, with different state functions distributed across multiple cities. Ancient Amaravati's Buddhist sculptures are now housed in museums worldwide, including the British Museum.

questions.question: Bhopal became internationally infamous due to which industrial disaster?
options: The Union Carbide gas leak of December 1984 — the world's worst industrial disaster

questions.question: The Bhopal gas tragedy killed how many people immediately and how many from long-term effects?
options: 2,259 immediately (officially), with estimates of 15,000-25,000 total deaths

questions.question: Madhya Pradesh is India's largest state by area. What is its approximate area?
The Bhimkund in Madhya Pradesh and the Bhimbetka rock shelters are in which broader region?
Bhopal is known for which traditional craft?

pins.summary: Bhopal — Madhya Pradesh's capital — is indelibly associated with the Union Carbide gas leak of December 3, 1984 — the world's worst industrial disaster. Methyl isocyanate gas escaping from the plant's storage tank killed at least 2,259 people immediately (some estimates put total deaths at 15,000-25,000 from long-term effects). Contaminated soil and groundwater continue to affect communities around the abandoned plant decades later. The disaster prompted fundamental changes to industrial safety regulation globally. Beyond this tragedy, Bhopal is a city of lakes (created by the 11th-century Paramara king Raja Bhoj), significant Mughal-era monuments, and traditional crafts including Zardozi embroidery and Bagh print textiles. Madhya Pradesh, India's largest state by area at 308,000 sq km, is rich in forests, minerals, and heritage sites.

questions.question: Goa's liberation from Portuguese rule occurred via which Indian military operation?
In which year was Goa liberated?
Goa achieved full statehood (separated from Daman and Diu) in which year?
Goa has India's highest per capita income among states. Its economy is driven primarily by?
options: Tourism, pharmaceuticals, and iron ore mining

questions.question: The Portuguese-era Fontainhas quarter of Panaji is famous for?
options: Its Latin Quarter of narrow lanes with tile-faced 19th-century Portuguese houses

pins.summary: Goa — liberated from 451 years of Portuguese rule by Indian military force (Operation Vijay) in December 1961 — achieved full statehood in 1987. India's smallest state by area (3,702 sq km), Goa has the country's highest per capita income, driven by its enormous tourism industry (over 7 million visitors annually), pharmaceutical manufacturing, and iron ore mining (though iron ore exports have been repeatedly restricted due to environmental concerns). Panaji's Fontainhas Latin Quarter — narrow cobblestone lanes flanked by tile-faced Portuguese colonial houses in yellow, blue, and green — is one of India's most distinctive urban heritage neighbourhoods. The Kochi-Goa coastal stretch has become India's most popular domestic tourism destination.

questions.question: Sikkim became India's 22nd state through what process in 1975?
options: A UN-supervised referendum followed by a vote in the Sikkim Assembly

questions.question: Sikkim's merger with India is still contested by which country?
options: China — which did not recognise Sikkim as part of India until 2003

questions.question: Pelling in West Sikkim offers views of which mountain?
Sikkim became India's first fully organic state in which year?
The Kanchenjunga National Park and Biosphere Reserve in Sikkim became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in which year?

pins.summary: Sikkim's integration into India in 1975 is one of modern history's most contested territorial incorporations. After a referendum (in which Sikkimese voted to join India) and a vote in the Sikkim Assembly, India's parliament passed the 36th Constitutional Amendment making Sikkim India's 22nd state. China did not recognise Sikkim as Indian territory until 2003 — a recognition that came partly through diplomatic negotiations. Pelling in West Sikkim offers some of the Himalayas' most dramatic mountain views, particularly of Kangchenjunga (8,586m), India's highest peak. The Kanchenjunga National Park became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016 — one of the few UNESCO sites in India for its 'Outstanding Universal Value' in both natural heritage and its association with Tibetan Buddhist culture.

questions.question: Haryana was created from Punjab in which year?

pins.summary: Haryana — carved from Punjab in 1966 along linguistic lines — shares Chandigarh as capital with Punjab in an arrangement that continues to generate periodic political friction (Haryana desires its own capital, Chandigarh). Haryana has been central to India's agricultural transformation: Green Revolution high-yielding wheat and paddy varieties, adopted first in Punjab-Haryana, made India food self-sufficient in the 1970s-80s. Kurukshetra in Haryana — believed to be the Mahabharata's battlefield — draws millions to the Brahma Sarovar tank during solar eclipses, considered one of Hinduism's most auspicious bathing occasions. Haryana consistently produces disproportionate numbers of Olympic wrestling and boxing champions from its rural belt.
